source.title: Genome-Factory: An Integrated Library for Tuning, Deploying, and Interpreting Genomic Models
source.authors: Wei-Min Wu; Xue-Feng Song; Yi-Bo Wen; Qinjie Lin; Zhi-Han Zhou; Jerry Yao-Chieh Hu; Zhong Wang; Han Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study presents sparse-autoencoder interpretation of genomic-model representations. It does not test the stated claims about language-model neuron poles, explanation accuracy, or neuron-based attribution graphs.
record.gate_note: The paper reports correlations between three sparse-autoencoder latent dimensions and sequence length, a CTCF-binding probe result, and accuracy changes after zeroing latent dimensions. These concern learned SAE latents in genomic models, not the model's own neuron poles or any of the specified versions; they are recorded as adjacent findings with versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: A genomic-model software library paper. Its interpretability section trains an SAE on DNABERT-2 embeddings and correlates SAE latents with sequence length and CTCF binding. It does not audit the model's own neurons, does not score explanations by simulating activations, and does not build neuron-based attribution graphs. No version is tested. The paper does not discuss the claim's sources at all, so 'discusses' overstates the relation; it neither tests nor uses the finding.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors present Genome-Factory as a unified library for tuning, deploying and interpreting genomic models. They say its SAE interpreter links latent features to genomic properties, and call it an initial step, not a fully validated tool for biological discovery.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a sparse autoencoder on genomic-model embeddings, then regression or classification and latent ablation; it does not audit language-model neuron poles or test explanations on held-out activations.

fits_no_version.finding: In DNABERT-2, three SAE latents (382, 519, 3519) correlate strongly with sequence length; the magnitude is not given. Zeroing SAE latents 2939, 3184 and 10 lowers CTCF probe accuracy (0.7881 before zeroing) by about 0.02 each.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse-autoencoder latents learned on genomic foundation-model embeddings can track sequence-level properties and regulatory signals.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: For the SAE interpretation results, the sequence-length correlations are described as strong but no correlation magnitudes or uncertainty are reported. The authors characterize the interpreter as an initial step rather than a fully validated biological-discovery tool.

untested.parts: Shares across language models and scale; the only models here are genomic models, and only SAE latents are examined
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron and recursive generalization
Effect of architecture, regularization and tools on interpretable-neuron share
Neuron-based attribution graphs without a replacement model
Simulation-based automated scoring of neuron explanations

record.verdict_notes: The reader set the relation to 'discusses'. 'cites_only' or a plain T6 fits better, since the paper never addresses neuron interpretability claims. The paper calls SAE units 'neurons', but these are SAE latents on final-layer embeddings, not model neurons, so they cannot bear on V1 or V2.

versions.untested_parts: Qwen3-32B audit shares for neuron poles.
Shares across language models, architectures, and model scales.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example and recursive generalization.
Effects of architecture, regularization, and tools on neuron interpretability shares.
Whether attribution graphs using a large model's own neurons explain behavior without a replacement model.
Whether explanations from activating examples predict where neurons fire on unseen activations.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.note: This evaluates SAE latents for a genomic classification task, not neuron explanation quality.
rows.check: Probe accuracy on SAE latents is a downstream classification score, not a measure of neuron interpretability. It is a property of the study's own tool and is better treated as context, not a result on the claim.
